cards.name: All Layers
cards.summary: Rasterizes every layer in the document that still holds vector or generated data (type, shape and fill layers, smart objects and similar) in one step, so each becomes an ordinary pixel layer. Nothing is selected first. The harvest found it enabled only when the document had a type layer or a smart object layer.
use_for: flattening a finished poster or social post to plain pixel layers before handing the PSD to a printer or an app that cannot read live type or smart objects
removing missing-font and linked-file warnings from a template before sharing it
preparing a layered comp for pixel-only work (painting, liquify, clone) across all layers at once
avoid: any file you may still edit: text stops being editable and smart objects lose their quality-safe scaling. Rasterize a duplicate, or save a layered master first
rasterizing only one layer: use Layer/Rasterize/Layer (or the specific Type / Shape / Smart Object item)
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('rasterizeAll'), new ActionDescriptor(), DialogModes.NO); verified live (a type layer became a pixel layer, history state 'Rasterize All Layers').

cards.name: Fill Content
cards.summary: Rasterizes only the fill of a fill or shape layer (solid colour, gradient or pattern) into pixels, while any vector mask stays a vector mask and the layer's mask is kept. Meant for a fill or shape layer: the harvest's menu-state scan had none, so it showed disabled in every state tried, but the call run on a Color Fill layer turned it into a normal pixel layer with its layer mask intact.
use_for: turning a gradient or pattern fill layer into pixels so it can be painted on, smudged or filtered
keeping a crisp vector edge on a shape while texturing its fill with filters or brushes
avoid: fills you may still recolour: double-click the fill layer thumbnail to change it instead, or keep a copy
rasterizing the whole shape including its outline: use Layer/Rasterize/Shape or Layer/Rasterize/Layer
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('rasterizeLayer'), desc, DialogModes.NO) with desc: null = reference to the target layer (Lyr), What = enum rasterizeItem 'content'; verified live on a Color Fill layer (layer kind fill -> pixel, mask kept, history 'Rasterize Fill Content'). DOM alternative (in the PS API harvest, not run): app.activeDocument.activeLayer.rasterize(RasterizeType.FILLCONTENT).

review.changes: summary: 'Enabled with a fill or shape layer selected' was never observed (disabled in every scanned state, none had a fill layer); now says so; script_api: added the RasterizeType.FILLCONTENT DOM route from the PS API harvest (not run)

cards.name: Generative
cards.summary: Rasterizes a generative layer (the layer type that Firefly features such as Generative Fill create) into an ordinary pixel layer, which as far as is known drops the layer's stored variations and generation settings. Not exercised by the harvest: it was disabled in every scratch state tried because none had a generative layer.
use_for: locking in the chosen Generative Fill result so the layer behaves like normal pixels for retouching and filters
shrinking a PSD that carries many generative variations before handing it off
avoid: layers whose other variations you may still want to compare: pick the variation first in the Properties panel, then rasterize
relying on exact behaviour in a script: there is no harvested script route
cards.script_api: No script route harvested (not run: no generative layer in the fixtures). No object-model call for it is known.

cards.name: Layer
cards.summary: Rasterizes all vector and live data on the selected layer or layers (live type, a shape and its vector mask, a fill, a smart object) into plain pixels in one go, whatever kind of layer it is. Layer styles stay live. The harvest found it enabled with a type or smart object layer selected and saw a type layer become a pixel layer.
use_for: turning a headline into pixels so it can be warped with Liquify, smudged or painted
making a placed logo or shape editable with brushes, filters and the Eraser
one command that works on any layer kind in a script, instead of picking Type / Shape / Smart Object
avoid: text you may still retype: duplicate the type layer and hide the original first
baking the drop shadow or stroke into pixels too: that is Layer/Rasterize/Layer Style
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('rasterizeLayer'), desc, DialogModes.NO) with desc: null = reference to the target layer (Lyr) and no What key; verified live on a type layer (history 'Rasterize Layer'). DOM alternative (unverified): app.activeDocument.activeLayer.rasterize(RasterizeType.ENTIRELAYER).

cards.name: Layer Style
cards.summary: Bakes the layer's effects (drop shadow, stroke, glow, bevel, overlays and so on) into the layer's own pixels and removes the live style, so the look stays the same but can no longer be edited from the Layer Style dialog. Needs a layer with a layer style (the menu-state scan had none, so it showed disabled in every state tried); in the harvest, run on a layer given an effect, the fx disappeared and the pixel bounds were rewritten.
use_for: freezing a text or logo effect so it survives export to apps that do not read Photoshop layer styles
painting, warping or masking the shadow and glow of a style as pixels
removing style-scaling surprises before resizing a layer
avoid: effects you may still tweak: keep the styled layer hidden as a backup or convert it to a smart object instead
a style on a type or shape layer you still need live: this bakes the whole layer, so rasterize a duplicate
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('rasterizeLayer'), desc, DialogModes.NO) with desc: null = reference to the target layer (Lyr), What = enum rasterizeItem 'layerStyle'; verified live (fx on -> off, history 'Rasterize Layer Style').

review.changes: summary: 'Enabled with a styled layer' was never observed (disabled in every scanned state); now says so

cards.name: Shape
cards.summary: Rasterizes a whole shape layer, fill and vector outline alike, into a normal pixel layer, so the shape can be painted or filtered but no longer edited as a path or rescaled crisply. Not exercised by the harvest: the fixtures had no shape layer, so it was disabled in every state tried.
use_for: turning a vector icon or badge into pixels to add grunge, texture or Liquify distortion
making a shape layer behave like a normal layer for filters that refuse vector layers
avoid: shapes you will resize later: scale first, or convert to a smart object to keep them crisp
keeping the vector outline: use Layer/Rasterize/Fill Content, which rasterizes only the fill

Same command as Layer/Smart Objects/Rasterize; enabled with a smart object layer selected.
use_for: making a placed photo or logo paintable with brushes, the Eraser or the clone tools
finalising a mock-up layer before Liquify or other edits that need plain pixels
cutting PSD size by dropping a heavy embedded source once the layout is final
avoid: layers you might still scale up or edit at source: rasterize a copy instead
unpacking a smart object back into its original layers: use Layer/Smart Objects/Convert to Layers

cards.name: Type
cards.summary: Rasterizes the live text of a type layer into pixels, so the text is no longer editable or font-dependent but can be painted, warped and filtered like any image; other vector data on the layer is left alone. Same command as Type/Rasterize Type Layer; enabled with a type layer selected.
use_for: distressing or texturing a headline with brushes, filters or Liquify
sending a PSD to someone who lacks the font, after the copy is final
breaking a word into pieces to animate or offset individual letters as pixels
avoid: copy that may still change: duplicate the type layer and hide the original first
only adding a stroke, shadow or warp: layer styles and Type > Warp Text work on live type

cards.name: Vector Mask
cards.summary: Converts the selected layer's vector mask (a path-based mask) into an ordinary pixel layer mask with the same shape, so its edge can be painted, blurred or feathered with brushes; the vector path is removed. In the harvest the vector mask became a layer mask and the document's path count dropped from 1 to 0.
use_for: softening or hand-painting part of a crisp path cut-out edge (hair, fur, shadows)
combining a pen-tool cut-out with brushed refinements in one mask
avoid: masks you will still reshape or rescale: keep the vector mask and feather it from the Properties panel instead
a layer that already has a pixel layer mask you need to keep separate: the result merges into one layer mask

retouching a single video frame with tools that refuse video layers
avoid: keeping the motion: rasterize a duplicate (Layer/Duplicate Layer) and keep the original video layer

cards.how: Choose it with one layer selected, type the new name and confirm it (the harvest found it disabled with several layers selected). Double-clicking the layer name in the Layers panel does the same.
use_for: naming layers clearly (headline, product, bg) so templates and hand-offs are readable
giving layers the names a script, data-driven variables or Export As layer names rely on
avoid: renaming many layers at once: do it in a script loop over the layers
renaming a document or file: use File > Save As

cards.summary: Deletes every smart filter (and the filter mask) from the selected smart object, returning it to its unfiltered look. In the harvest a Gaussian Blur smart filter was removed and the layer's bounds shrank back to the original (history 'Delete All Smart Filters').

cards.summary: Deletes the mask that limits where the smart filters of the selected smart object apply, so the filters affect the whole layer again; the filters themselves stay. Verified in the harvest (history 'Delete Filter Mask').

cards.name: Convert to Layers
cards.summary: Unpacks the selected smart object back into the ordinary layers it contains, placed in the document in its stead, so the contents can be edited directly without opening a separate document. In the harvest a smart object became a normal pixel layer (history 'Convert Smart Object to Layers').
use_for: breaking open a smart-object logo lock-up or text block to restyle its parts in place
flattening the nesting of a template whose smart objects are no longer needed
avoid: smart objects shared by several instances you want to keep in sync: edit with Layer/Smart Objects/Edit Contents instead
only needing pixels: Layer/Smart Objects/Rasterize gives one flat layer

cards.name: Convert to Linked
cards.summary: Writes the contents of an embedded smart object out to a file on disk and turns the layer into a linked smart object pointing at that file, so other documents can link to the same source and the PSD gets smaller. Opens a save dialog for the file name and location (menu title 'Convert to Linked...'). The harvest found the menu item enabled in every scratch state, including ones without a smart object.
cards.how: Pick a folder and file name in the save dialog; the contents are saved in their native format (usually .psb for content made in Photoshop). After that the layer shows the link icon, and editing the file updates every document that links to it.
use_for: sharing one logo or product shot across many campaign PSDs so a single edit updates them all
shrinking a heavy PSD by moving large embedded sources out to files
avoid: files that must travel as one self-contained PSD: links break when the folder moves; package or keep embedded
only saving a copy of the contents: use Layer/Smart Objects/Export Contents
cards.script_api: app.runMenuItem(stringIDToTypeID('placedLayerConvertToLinked')) is the terminology label match (not run: it opens a save dialog). No no-dialog route was harvested.

cards.name: Convert to Smart Object
cards.summary: Wraps the selected layer or layers into one embedded smart object, which keeps the original pixels or vectors inside so later scaling, warps and filters (as smart filters) stay editable and lossless. Needs an open document with a layer selected; in the harvest a pixel layer became a smart object.
use_for: applying editable smart filters (blur, sharpen, Camera Raw) to a photo
scaling a logo or product shot up and down while laying out a poster without losing quality
turning a group of layers into one placeable unit for mock-ups and templates
avoid: layers you need to paint on directly: brushes and the Eraser do not work on a smart object (edit its contents or rasterize)
a copy that must stay independent: use Layer/Smart Objects/New Smart Object via Copy rather than Layer/New/Layer Via Copy (whose copies share contents)
cards.script_api: app.runMenuItem(stringIDToTypeID('newPlacedLayer')); verified live (pixel layer -> smart object, history 'Convert to Smart Object'). executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('newPlacedLayer'), undefined, DialogModes.NO) is the common Action Manager form (unverified).

review.changes: avoid: Ctrl+J is not in this batch (the harvest binds it to Layer/New/Layer Via Copy); named the command by its harvested path

cards.how: Edit the opened document, then save (not Save As) and close it to push the change back into the parent PSD. Linked smart objects open their linked file instead.
use_for: changing the artwork inside a mock-up's screen or label placeholder
editing a logo once and having every instance in the layout update
retouching a photo that is already scaled and filtered in the layout without losing those transforms
avoid: swapping in a different file entirely: use Layer/Smart Objects/Replace Contents
scripts that expect the active document to stay the same: the contents document becomes active
